standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the defining condition making the data of a sheaf map into an f-map.

core_obligations: (1)<->(3): a sheaf map a : G \to f_*F is a family a_V : G(V) \to F(f^{-1}(V)) (pushforward computed as F(f^{-1}(V))), and a is a sheaf map exactly when the family satisfies the f-map condition of Definition definition-f-map (proof lines 2482-2496). (2)<->(4): f^{-1}G is the sheafification of f_pG, so a sheaf map b : f^{-1}G \to F is a presheaf map b_p : f_pG \to F, i.e. compatible maps b_{p,U} : colim_{f(U) \subset V} G(V) \to F(U), i.e. collections b_{p,U,V} : G(V) \to F(U) compatible with all restriction maps; conversely such a collection defines b_p and b (proof lines 2498-2516). (3)<->(4): forgetting structure sends an f-map xi to xi_{U,V} = the composition of xi_V : G(V) \to F(f^{-1}(V)) with the restriction F(f^{-1}(V)) \to F(U), well defined because f(U) \subset V (proof lines 2518-2523).
proof_roadmap: Identify (1) with (3) through the pushforward description and the f-map definition (proof lines 2482-2496).
Identify (2) with (4) through the universal property of sheafification (proof lines 2498-2516).
Identify (3) with (4) by the explicit forgetting-structure composition (proof lines 2518-2523).
